hints: Notice the position of the functional group moves from carbon 1 in the alcohol to carbon 2 in the bromoalkane, so this cannot be a simple direct swap.
Remember that concentrated sulfuric acid dehydrates a primary alcohol to form an alkene, in this case but-1-ene (which can rearrange to but-2-ene).
Think about which reagent adds to a C=C double bond to place H on one carbon and Br on the more stable carbocation carbon to give the 2-bromo product.
walkthrough:
**Spot the skeleton change**

Look closely at the starting material and product. You start with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and you want $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3$. The Br is not in the same place as the OH was.

This tells you a direct nucleophilic substitution will not work, because that would give 1-bromobutane.

**Dehydrate first to make an alkene**

Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent and eliminates water from butan-1-ol to form butene.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Add HBr by electrophilic addition**

Hydrogen bromide adds across the C=C double bond by Markovnikov addition. The H adds to the carbon with more H atoms already, and Br adds to the more stable secondary carbocation to give 2-bromobutane.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3$$

**Choose the two-step sequence**

So you need dehydration followed by hydrobromination. That is concentrated sulfuric acid followed by hydrogen bromide.

options.A: Bromine with UV light causes free radical substitution of alkanes, not alcohols. It would give a mixture of bromination products and does not involve the OH group chemistry needed here.
options.B: Concentrated sulfuric acid with KBr generates HBr in situ which directly substitutes OH by Br in a primary alcohol. This is an $S_N2$ type replacement with no rearrangement, so it gives 1-bromobutane, not 2-bromobutane.
options.C: The first step correctly makes butene, but $\text{Br}_2$ adds across the double bond to give a dibromoalkane. You would get 1,2-dibromobutane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$), not the monobromo product.
options.D: This is the correct two-step route. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dehydrates butan-1-ol to butene, then HBr undergoes Markovnikov electrophilic addition to place Br on carbon 2, forming 2-bromobutane.
